consensus_summary: The 'new name' symbolizes a God-conferred transformed identity, character, and status (with belonging, vindication, and destiny) given to the redeemed or overcomer, drawn from biblical renaming patterns and Revelation promises; secondary readings (ownership mark, secret intimacy, admission token, corporate Zion, or Christ's own name) are treated as complementary or minority variants around that core.
book_summary: A renewed Word, covenant, and priesthood that is known, received, and kept only by the one who bears the renewed Name.
consensus_core_identification: God-bestowed new personal/corporate identity, character, and status on the redeemed/overcomer.
book_core_identification: Renewed Word, covenant, and priesthood (personally known/received/kept by its bearer).
boundary_disagreement: Consensus alternatives stay within identity/status/ownership/intimacy/token/corporate-name readings of the same renaming texts; none extend the referent to Word, covenant, or priesthood as the name itself.
material_contradiction: None directly asserted; the book simply identifies a different primary referent without explicitly denying the identity reading it labels 'commonly taught.'
rationale: Minimum cores differ in kind: consensus (and every listed alternative) centers on a transformed identity/status conferred on persons or Zion, while the book equates the new name with a renewed Word-covenant-priesthood complex known only to the bearer. No consensus primary or alternative covers that identification, yielding novelty rather than refinement or contradiction of a shared referent.
strongest_objection: The printed texts (Gen 32:28; Isa 62:2-5; 65:15; Rev 2:17) are the standard identity-renaming passages and supply no explicit warrant for equating the new name with Word, covenant, or priesthood.
